title: File paths and text encoding

spans.text: WHY USE THIS?
Pathlib builds platform-aware paths; hardcoded separators can behave differently on another operating system.
CORE EXPLANATION
Build platform-independent paths with pathlib. Setting encoding='utf-8' when opening text files makes encoding behavior explicit.
EXAMPLE CODE
QUESTION: What will this code print? Predict first, then run it.

spans.code:
from pathlib import Path

path = Path('data') / 'notes.txt'
path.write_text('Salam', encoding='utf-8')

spans.text: EXPECTED RESULT

spans.code: No console output; creates data/notes.txt containing Salam.

spans.text:

`path = Path('data') / 'notes.txt'` — Binds the evaluated expression to a name; without the assignment, later lines cannot reuse that result.
`path.write_text('Salam', encoding='utf-8')` — Writes the supplied text to the file, replacing its existing contents; the encoding is explicit.

spans.title: Why it matters
spans.text: Pathlib builds platform-aware paths; hardcoded separators can behave differently on another operating system.

spans.title: Watch out
spans.text: Paths and permissions can fail; validate untrusted contents and handle parse errors.
COMMON MISTAKES
Use
with
for files, choose an encoding explicitly, and validate external data.
